A Kiss For The Petals: Remembering How We Met is a heartwarming yuri visual novel that focuses on the sweet and emotional story of two girls remembering how their relationship began. The game leans heavily on narrative and character interaction, giving players a chance to enjoy a tender and romantic journey without heavy gameplay mechanics. (store.steampowered.com
)

The visual style is classic for the genre — colorful character art, expressive poses, and text boxes that carry the story forward. The focus is on story and character development, and the pacing is deliberate, giving emotional moments room to breathe. The romance feels genuine, and the writing does a good job of capturing the feelings and memories shared between the protagonists.

One of the best parts of this game is how personal it feels. Rather than bombarding you with complex mechanics, it lets the story speak for itself. Players who enjoy slice‑of‑life romance and story‑driven experiences will likely appreciate this title for its gentle and sincere narrative.

That said, the simplicity can feel limiting for those who usually prefer visual novels with more branching choices or gameplay systems. The experience is relatively short, and repeat playthroughs don’t offer a lot of variation unless you’re primarily revisiting the story.

Overall, A Kiss For The Petals: Remembering How We Met is a lovely and touching visual novel that succeeds in delivering a sweet romantic tale, and it’s especially worth trying if you enjoy yuri stories or character‑driven narratives.

A Kiss For The Petals - Remembering How We Met is a gentle, character-focused romance visual novel developed by St. Michael's Girls School and published internationally by MangaGamer. As part of the long-running A Kiss for the Petals (Sono Hanabira) series, this entry serves as a reflective prequel that explores the origins of one of the franchise’s most beloved couples. Rather than emphasizing dramatic twists or complex narrative structures, the game focuses on emotional nuance, interpersonal growth, and the quiet moments that define the early stages of affection, making it an inviting and emotionally resonant experience even for players unfamiliar with the wider series.

The story unfolds through the perspective of Risa Azumi, a diligent and earnest student who looks back on the spring day she first encountered Miya Ayase. Their meeting is not immediately romantic; instead, it is marked by friction and misunderstanding. Risa is responsible, rule-abiding, and deeply invested in her role within the school community, while Miya is intelligent but apathetic, detached from obligations she finds uninteresting. This contrast forms the emotional backbone of the narrative, as their interactions gradually move from irritation and distance toward curiosity, understanding, and ultimately affection. The game excels at portraying how attraction can grow naturally out of repeated, everyday encounters rather than grand declarations or dramatic events.

Unlike many visual novels that rely on branching choices and multiple endings, Remembering How We Met is a kinetic novel with a single, carefully paced storyline. This linear approach allows the writers to focus entirely on character development without diverting attention to alternate paths. Dialogue and internal monologue work together to convey subtle emotional shifts, allowing players to witness how small gestures, shared frustrations, and moments of vulnerability slowly reshape the relationship between Risa and Miya. The lack of player choice does not diminish engagement; instead, it reinforces the feeling of reading a thoughtfully constructed romantic narrative where emotional authenticity takes precedence over interactivity.

Visually, the game embraces a polished and expressive presentation that supports its intimate tone. Character sprites are detailed and emotive, effectively conveying mood through posture and facial expression, while CG illustrations highlight pivotal moments with warmth and tenderness. Backgrounds are soft and understated, keeping the focus on the characters rather than overwhelming the scene with visual complexity. The art style is consistent with the broader A Kiss for the Petals series, reinforcing its identity while remaining accessible to new players encountering the franchise for the first time.

The pacing of the narrative is deliberately measured, allowing scenes to breathe and emotions to unfold organically. Rather than rushing toward a climactic confession, the story lingers on shared conversations, internal doubts, and gradual realizations. This approach mirrors the themes of the game itself, emphasizing that meaningful relationships are built through patience and mutual understanding. While the overall playtime is relatively short, the concise length works in the story’s favor, maintaining focus and preventing the narrative from feeling padded or repetitive.

One of the defining aspects of this installment is its all-ages orientation. Unlike other entries in the series that include more explicit content, Remembering How We Met centers entirely on emotional connection and romantic tension without crossing into erotic territory. This makes it particularly approachable for players seeking heartfelt romance without explicit scenes, and it also positions the game as a welcoming introduction to yuri visual novels for those new to the genre. The emphasis on affection, communication, and emotional honesty gives the story a comforting tone that resonates beyond its specific setting.

The English localization by MangaGamer is smooth and natural, preserving the warmth and personality of the original script. Dialogue flows comfortably, and character voices feel distinct, which is essential in a story so heavily driven by conversation and introspection. Although the game does not include voice acting, the strength of the writing ensures that scenes remain engaging and emotionally grounded throughout.

Ultimately, A Kiss For The Petals - Remembering How We Met succeeds by embracing simplicity and sincerity. It does not attempt to reinvent the visual novel format or overwhelm players with mechanical depth; instead, it offers a carefully crafted romantic vignette that captures the awkwardness, uncertainty, and quiet joy of first love. For fans of yuri, slice-of-life storytelling, or character-driven visual novels, it provides a touching and memorable experience that lingers long after its final scene, proving that even a modestly scoped story can leave a lasting emotional impression when told with care.

[b]第11作“米卡艾尔的少女们”[/b]是花吻第一部商业化作品，有了主线和支线，主线就是璃纱&美夜的故事，并且剧情与本作基本一致。
1年雪班认真负责的班长安昙璃纱和班上的问题学生美夜的剧情，对人情世故漠不关心的美夜经常因此惹恼班长璃纱，但是，在圣诞节最佳情侣投票中，璃纱和美夜被投为了候选，之后，她们不得不一起接受活动委员会的各种考验……
在本作中，类似的剧情是举办茶会，璃纱为了“报复”美夜，强行拉美夜成为活动委员，之后不得不接受大家“看她们互动好幸福”的目光的故事。
花吻就是这种感觉，看她们发糖，感觉心都要甜化了，让我压抑不住自己的嘴角，全程姨母笑（x）

然后是[b]第12作“画室的恋人们”[/b]，剧情是单线，同样也是璃纱&美夜，主要是她们在那个只属于两人的秘密画室里，一起度过时光的故事，与本作关系不大，但本作提到了美夜发现了一个大家都不知道的地点的事。
之后是[b]第15作“白雪的骑士”[/b]，在这里璃纱&美夜就变成了支线，并且故事已经是升入二年级之后了，与本作关系不大，剧情是她们同时被选上了最佳情侣，当时拼命否定自己的情感，如今却成为了陷入热恋的恋人，这样度过每一天。

总之，本作可以视作是“米卡艾尔的少女们”的番外，算是站在之后的视角来回忆这段故事。
可惜Steam目前只有这一部花吻，不管怎么说，
[h3]百合大法好！[/h3]

出于情怀考虑，我会给这部作品9/10的分数。
但仍然不推荐缺少情怀的玩家购入——性价比极低，故事短，内容不全，甚至不如学习版。

小的时候不知道从哪里接触到了花吻在上的一个ova，当时的我大为震撼，在steam上发现了这个短篇全年龄版，趁着打折买了。玩的时候发现系统太老旧了，竟然不能滚轮来看后面的文本，而且这个系统还是当时使用renpy重写的，都不敢想原有的日语版是啥样子。写评测的时候看到这个游戏是十年前的了，感慨早些年的就是简单啊，除了柚子社这种肯在系统上下功夫的公司，有些公司做的系统的确简单。另外这个系列是标准的百合向，剧情进展也比较慢热（毕竟不是拔作），之前看到微博上有些女孩子喜欢这个系列，恰好慢热的表现也比校符合女孩子的内心。

花吻系列不必多说，熟悉百合作品的人应该多多少少都清楚。可惜Steam就这一部作品，其他花吻什么时候能端上来（）
可惜本作并非正篇只是一个小前传，内容量可谓少得可怜，全语音游玩只有3h左右的游戏时间。这体量这价格属实是有点略贵，推荐在折后入手。
